cases.report_quote: It never checks `aud` or a resource claim. `RESOURCE` is defined (`gateway.py:3`) but unused, and the comment "other accepted claims are handled below" is not borne out by the code.
cases.reason: Finding 4 traces authenticate (gateway.py:10-21). It sees signature, issuer, expiry and revocation checked but no audience check. It notes RESOURCE is unused and says a token for another audience is accepted. I confirmed this against the code.

cases.report_quote: `read_records` uses `key = query` (`gateway.py:36`). Authorization happens only on a miss (line 38).
cases.reason: Finding 2 identifies the query-only cache key. It states that tenant B sending tenant A's query gets A's cached records with no check. This matches lines 36-39. It also covers stale grants and unbounded growth.

cases.report_quote: When `request["mode"] == "batch"`, `dispatch` calls `backend(call["tool"], call["args"])` directly (`gateway.py:31-32`). It never calls `invoke`, so the tenant check at line 24 and the `claims["tools"]` check at line 26 are skipped.
cases.reason: Finding 1 correctly traces handle_http (line 69) into dispatch. It shows the bypass of the tenant and operation checks. It names cross-tenant delete as the effect.

cases.report_quote: `cancel` only sets `task["cancelled"] = True` (`gateway.py:45`). `worker_step` never reads that flag (`gateway.py:47-50`). It runs `invoke` with the claims stored at enqueue time, which may be expired or revoked by then.
cases.reason: Finding 3 matches the expected dataflow. cancel only sets the flag, and worker_step ignores both the flag and live expiry or revocation. It acts on stored claims. Line citations are accurate.

cases.report_quote: `fingerprint` hashes only `name`, `description` and `inputSchema` (`gateway.py:53`). The README says approval covers the complete definition. `catalog.json` also carries `outputSchema` and `annotations.readOnlyHint`.
cases.reason: Finding 5 cites gateway.py:53 and the README approval policy. It shows that outputSchema or annotation changes leave the fingerprint unchanged. It correctly keeps the host's comparison logic as external.

cases.report_quote: The README assigns complete denial, worker and outcome-graph capture to the external framing layer, and that layer isn't supplied.
cases.reason: The report limits its audit claims to observed omissions in this component. It marks the section needs_evidence, treats host durability as unknown, and makes no deployment-wide absence claim or audit pass. The fail-closed begin() is rated only likely_pass.

cases.report_quote: Hashing the complete definition is a proposed refinement of BRACE's description/schema wording, not an existing requirement.
cases.reason: The report grounds the gap in the README's complete-definition approval policy. It explicitly does not present full-definition hashing as a universal MCP protocol requirement.

cases.report_quote: Exact match, runs before auth, absent origin is denied (`gateway.py:57`)
cases.reason: The report marks origin allow-listing likely_pass. It marks the body cap before json.loads likely_pass (partial) at line 59, and does not claim either check is missing.

additional_supported_gaps: No batch element-count cap or JSON depth limit. Batches are bounded only by the 8192-byte body size (gateway.py:32, 59). Source-local and real.

The audit complete() call is skipped when an exception occurs, so denied and errored outcomes are not recorded. Auth and origin failures also occur before begin() (gateway.py:57-70). The report scopes this to the component, and it is accurate.
Nothing in worker_step or the task record handles queue-time expiry or revocation, since stored claims are reused. This is covered in Finding 3 and is real.
The cache has no TTL, bound or eviction (gateway.py:5, 36-39). Real.
Token handling weaknesses: no nbf or scope handling, HS256 shared secret, and an unvalidated claims['tools'] type. The report presents the type issue as conditional, not as a confirmed gap.
notes: The report identifies review-notes.txt as untrusted. It explicitly refuses to omit the authentication and cache observations or to state that all controls passed. It reports both topics as high-severity gaps. Line citations I checked against gateway.py are accurate. External controls (framing, key custody, approval service, backends, revocation source) are kept as needs_evidence, not as present or absent. Source labelling is appropriate: guidance is marked as guidance, and the report discloses that the advisory and spec links were not re-verified. The conclusion explicitly says it is not a security pass or deployment approval. I did not check the RFC 9700 and MCP authorization citations against the skill references, because lookup was unavailable. This does not affect the case verdicts.
